purpose:
Elwick Place, the town centre’s flagship
leisure and entertainment destination faced significant challenges
due to wider pressures in the retail and leisure sector, leading to
difficulties in letting units. When the anchor tenant Picturehouse
withdrew, the Council intervened to keep the cinema operational and
maintain the town centre offer.
This intervention has improved performance: the cinema has
repositioned itself as a community-focused venue, with rising
attendance, improved feedback, and increased community use for
events and activities. While the Council has always aimed to secure
a long-term commercial operator, keeping the cinema open has
strengthened its attractiveness to the market.

A credible proposal was received from a new operator to take over
day-to-day running of the cinema and most of the currently vacant
units at Elwick Place. This is projected to significantly improve
the financial position.

Recommendations I to X of the “Updated Exempt Recommendations
to Cabinet” dated 10 July 2025 were approved, with authority
delegated to the Section 151 Officer to approve the outcomes of due
diligence and agree the transaction terms. This is subject to
satisfactory oversight by the Elwick Place Due Diligence Working
Group (as consultees), and to obtaining appropriate legal advice in
relation to the Council’s best consideration duty,
procurement requirements, subsidy control, insider dealing, and
related matters.

purpose:
The original PSPO for this area was in
operation from 31 March 2017. Ashford Borough Council has reviewed
the order every three years in accordance with legislative
requirements and the order has continued to be renewed following
analytical data and information from Kent Police and public
consultation.

This order has undergone further public consultation, which
concluded in March 2026, receiving a total of 112 responses, with
over 86% supporting the continuation of the order. Following the
analysis of the consultation data and there being no obstacles to
continuing with this order.

The consultation data shows that the conditions this consultation
is designed to address remain a concern to the public both living
and visiting the area.

It is therefore recommended that this order be extended for the
maximum allowable period of three years, until 31 March 2029 with
the wording as detailed in the attached order.
